summary: Describes dynamic allocation of shared IPv4 addresses with DHCPv4. A single address can be given to multiple clients at once, each distinguished by a unique set of transport-layer source port numbers.

eli5.summary: Several people share one phone number, each with their own extension range.

questions: what is a shared ipv4 address
what is a port set id
subtitle: How a DHCP server can hand the same IPv4 address to many clients at once, each with its own range of ports.

tldr.problem: Operators do not always have enough public IPv4 addresses to give one to every connected device, especially while they move from native IPv4 to native IPv6 with IPv4 as an overlay service.
tldr.mechanism: A DHCP 4o6 server leases one IPv4 address to several clients at the same time and gives each a unique Port Set ID (PSID), carried in a new DHCPv4 option, OPTION_V4_PORTPARAMS (code 159). The address plus PSID pair identifies each lease.
tldr.outcome: Clients get a shared address limited to their own set of Layer 4 ports. This only suits certain architectures: point-to-point or authenticated links, and Address plus Port (A+P) designs.

today: RFC 7618 is a Proposed Standard from August 2015. The unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Share an IPv4 Address
sections.content:
There are not enough public IPv4 addresses to give a full one to every connected device. The RFC calls the problem particularly acute while an operator moves from a native IPv4 network to a native IPv6 network, with IPv4 offered as an overlay service. Public IPv4 addresses are then needed for both the existing and the transition networks.

Two kinds of solution have emerged: Carrier-Grade NAT devices (CGNs), or giving the same public IPv4 address to several clients that are told apart by non-overlapping Layer 4 port sets. This memo covers the second kind. It builds on the DHCP 4o6 server of RFC 7341, which leases IPv4 addresses as in DHCPv4 but carries the exchange inside DHCPv6 messages, and adds a new DHCPv4 option for shared leases.
sections.eli5: There are too few street addresses to go around. So instead of each house getting its own, several houses share one address and each gets its own set of door numbers.

sections.title: Where This Can Be Used
sections.content:
Because many hosts hold the same IP address, the address no longer identifies one host. The solution is therefore only suitable for architectures based on the Address plus Port model (A+P), namely RFC 7596 and certain configurations of RFC 7597 (for example, an Embedded Address bit length of 0).

It should only be used on point-to-point links, tunnels, or where link-layer authentication happens before an IP address is assigned. It is not suitable for network access over shared media such as Ethernet, WLAN or cable.
sections.eli5: Sharing one address only works when the mail carrier knows exactly which house is which, such as on a private road with a guard at the gate. It does not work in a crowded open square.

sections.title: Shared Addresses and Port Sets
sections.content:
A shared IPv4 address is an IPv4 address with a restricted Layer 4 port set. A Port Set ID (PSID) identifies the range of ports assigned to one DHCP client.

Allocation works like ordinary DHCPv4 leasing (RFC 2131), with one key difference: the server can give the same IPv4 address to more than one client at once, as long as each lease carries a unique port range. The combined tuple of IPv4 address and PSID must be unique for each active lease, so the server tracks leases by that pair rather than by address alone.

A client that supports the feature lists OPTION_V4_PORTPARAMS in the Parameter Request List of its DHCPDISCOVER and DHCPREQUEST messages. If it receives several offers and one is for a full IPv4 address (no OPTION_V4_PORTPARAMS), it SHOULD prefer that full address unless configured otherwise.
sections.eli5: The address is the building, and the port set is your apartment range. The building manager writes down both so two tenants never get the same apartment.

sections.title: The Client-Server Exchange
sections.content:
The DHCPv4 messages travel inside the DHCPv4-query and DHCPv4-response messages of RFC 7341. The steps are:

  • The client sends a DHCPDISCOVER with its client identifier and OPTION_V4_PORTPARAMS in the Parameter Request List. It MAY include the option with preferred values as a suggestion.
  • A server that supports shared addresses answers with a DHCPOFFER holding the shared address in yiaddr and, as a MUST, an OPTION_V4_PORTPARAMS with an available port set. If the client asked for a non-zero PSID length, the server MAY offer a port set of that size, depending on policy.
  • The client picks an offer and sends a DHCPREQUEST containing the OPTION_V4_PORTPARAMS it was offered.
  • The server creates a binding of client identifier, IPv4 address and PSID, and MUST reply with a DHCPACK containing the option.
  • The client MUST NOT run an in-use probe, such as ARPing, on the address.
  • To give up a lease, the client sends a DHCPRELEASE with the leased address and the option holding its PSID.

A client that stored its earlier address and port set follows the INIT-REBOOT logic of RFC 2131 as long as its DHCP 4o6 source IPv6 address has not changed. If that IPv6 address changes for any reason, it MUST start over with a DHCPDISCOVER.
sections.eli5: You ask for a room, the manager offers you one with a range of door numbers, you say yes, and she writes it down. Later you hand the key back and say which door numbers you had.

sections.title: Client and Server Rules
sections.content:
On the client, the option in the DHCPACK gives the explicit PSID to use for the interface. The client MUST apply the allocated ports to all traffic of the shared address: it MUST use only port-aware protocols (such as TCP, UDP and DCCP) and be ICMP compliant with RFC 5508; connections it starts MUST use a source port from its set; and it MUST NOT accept inbound connections on ports outside the set. It MUST NOT use the shared address for ARP, and if the DHCPv4-over-DHCPv6 mechanism fails it MUST NOT configure an IPv4 link-local address from 169.254.0.0/16. How the client enforces these rules is out of scope. If the reply has no OPTION_V4_PORTPARAMS, the client SHOULD configure a full IPv4 address with no sharing.

On the server, the option MUST NOT be sent unless the client listed it in the Parameter Request List. The server needs an address-and-port-set pool, and its lease database MUST include the IPv4 address, the PSID and the client identifier. To choose what to offer, it SHOULD try in order: the client's current binding, the client's previous binding if still free, the requested address and PSID if valid and free, and finally a new address with a PSID from the pool. The address and port set MUST be assigned in the same DHCP message. The server MUST be able to reserve some port ranges (for example 0-1023) from allocation, with a configurable policy.

A server serving both kinds of client MUST make sure clients without the option never get shared addresses, for example by using two separate pools. A server with only shared pools MUST discard requests lacking the option.
sections.eli5: Each tenant must stay in their own door numbers and may not borrow someone else's. The manager keeps one list of who has what, and keeps the lowest door numbers for the building itself.

sections.title: The Port Parameters Option
sections.content:
OPTION_V4_PORTPARAMS has option code 159 and option-len 4. Its offset, PSID-len and PSID fields mean the same as in the S46 Port Parameters option of RFC 7598, so existing port-set implementations stay compatible.

  • offset (8 bits): the number of excluded port range or offset bits ('a' bits). Allowed values are 0 to 15, with a default of 6 for MAP-based implementations. A Lightweight 4over6 client does not use it and it should be 0.
  • PSID-len (8 bits): the number of significant bits in the PSID, also called 'k'. When 0, the PSID field is ignored. The address-sharing ratio is 2^k.
  • PSID (16 bits): the explicit PSID. The first k bits on the left are the value and the remaining (16 - k) bits are padding zeros.

To keep system ports and operator-reserved ports out of clients' hands, port sets containing well-known ports MUST NOT be assigned unless the operator has explicitly configured otherwise, for example by allocating a full IPv4 address.
sections.eli5: The option is a small slip of paper with a few numbers on it. It tells you which door numbers are yours and how many tenants share the building.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The considerations of RFC 2131 and RFC 7341 also apply. Unauthorized DHCP 4o6 servers could stage an amplification attack or supply an invalid configuration that disrupts service. Using unicast DHCP 4o6 message flows reduces this risk.

A malicious user could request many addresses or port sets to exhaust the pool. The suggested mitigation is an allocation policy on each customer site that limits the number of simultaneously active IPv4 leases.

The client identifier keeps parameters stable but lets the server track the client, so clients can trade stability for privacy by controlling its value. Port randomization (RFC 6056) is harder because a host can only randomize within its fixed port range. The RFC advises other protections, such as the measures in RFC 5961 against blind in-window TCP attacks, or using IPv6.
sections.eli5: A fake manager could hand out wrong room numbers, and a greedy person could grab lots of rooms. Limiting how many rooms one household can have helps.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: IANA assigned one new DHCPv4 option code in its BOOTP and DHCP parameters registry: OPTION_V4_PORTPARAMS, tag 159, data length 4. Its meaning is to configure a set of ports bound to a shared IPv4 address.
sections.eli5: The official list of option numbers got one new entry, number 159, for the port-set slip.

fields.name: offset
fields.desc: Excluded port range or offset bits ('a'); 0 to 15, default 6 for MAP.

fields.name: PSID-len
fields.desc: Number of significant bits in the PSID ('k'); 0 means ignore the PSID.

fields.name: PSID
fields.desc: Port Set ID in the first k bits, padded with zeros.
